objections.gloss: The objection loses on the burden before any evidence is heard. A sex-role assigned at birth was assigned without the assignee's assent — and an ascription no one consented to cannot be the thing a…
objections.title: The burden is on the trans person to justify departing from their natal sex. Absent a successful justification — metaphysical (that one can change sex) or therapeutic (that intervention is medically necessary) — there is no right to transition; the default is to remain as assigned.

objections.gloss: The objection assumes the only non-arbitrary stopping rule must rest on a metaphysical truth about which identity is real, so that severing gender self-ID from a truth-maker leaves bare…
objections.title: Once identity is severed from any external truth-maker and grounded in bare self-declaration, no non-arbitrary principle distinguishes the gender self-ID you protect from species, age, or race self-ID, which you do not. Either protect all of them — absurd, and corrosive of the categories and resources others rely on — or your protection of gender self-ID is arbitrary special-pleading. Any line you draw either re-imports the metaphysics you conceded or is bare stipulation. So self-ID grounds no right.

objections.gloss: The objection states the wing's own defense in its final line: a self-regarding permission cannot generate a duty in me. Just so — and it does not. The right is a liberty over one's own name, body…
objections.title: A right to transition does not stay in its lane. To recognize it is to conscript others into its upkeep: it requires me to speak words I hold false, to affirm in my professional capacity — as doctor, counselor, employer — an identity I reject, and to alter the records and language I am responsible for. My own liberties — speech, conscience, association, professional judgment — are self-regarding too, and this right tramples them. So it is not the modest self-regarding permission it advertises; it is a claim on my participation. And a self-regarding permission cannot generate a duty in me.

objections.gloss: The objection's force is in one inference: the body is a gift, so you owe the giver its preservation un-altered, and to alter it is ingratitude. Grant that the body is a gift — the inference still…
objections.title: Your body was given to you — by God, by nature, by your parents — as a gift. To alter it is ingratitude and defacement: you owe the giver the body's preservation, un-altered. Gender-affirming alteration breaks that debt of gratitude and disrespects the source of the gift, so you have no right to it.

objections.gloss: Concede the whole primitive, arguendo: sex is a biological fact, and ‘inner gender as essence’ names nothing coherent or falsifiable. The right is still untouched, because its objects were never an…
objections.title: No coherent referent grounds the gender you claim to self-determine. Sex is a biological fact, binary and immutable; an inner gender-as-essence is incoherent and unfalsifiable, tracking no fact of the matter. So self-determination has no object — nothing real is determined — and you assert a falsehood others are then asked to encode in speech and record.
